The increasing width of the confidence intervals across the horizons directly reflects the accumulation of uncertainty over time. Outcomes could fall outside these stated intervals if highly impactful and unexpected events occur that significantly alter the fundamental landscape. Conversely, an unexpectedly strong economic boom, a breakthrough innovation, or the sudden resolution of a major long-standing uncertainty could drive outcomes above the upper bounds. These types of "black swan" events or fundamental shifts are difficult to predict and model within standard probabilistic frameworks, representing the primary risks to these forecasts.
